samples.text:
The plans show the ground floor of a shopping centre in 2010 and in 2024. Overall, the layout of the centre is same, but many shops have changed into places for food, leisure and services.

In both years, there is a central walkway from the west to the east with entrances at each end, and also a north entrance. On the north side of the walkway, the clothes shop and the supermarket did not change. However, the department store in the north-west became a food court and the bookshop was replaced with a phone shop.

On the south side, only the shoe shop is still there. The electronics shop in the south-west have been changed to a gym. The bank next to shoe shop is now parcel lockers and click-and-collect, and the travel agent became a pharmacy. Finally, the café in the south-east was replaced by a cinema. So in 2024 there are less traditional shops and more places for doing activities.
samples.why: Overview present but basic · all changes identified and grouped by side · repetitive linking and structures · adequate vocabulary · errors in articles, agreement and comparatives which do not block meaning.

samples.text:
The plans compare the ground floor of a shopping centre in 2010 and 2024. Overall, while the basic layout and the size of each unit have remained the same, the centre has moved away from traditional retail towards leisure, food and service outlets.

The central walkway, which runs from west to east with entrances at both ends and a third entrance in the north, is unchanged. Along its northern side, the clothes shop and the large supermarket in the north-east have been kept. However, the department store in the north-west has been converted into a food court, and the neighbouring bookshop has been taken over by a phone shop.

The southern side of the building has seen even more change, as the shoe shop is the only unit which still has the same use. The electronics store in the south-west has become a gym, while the bank in the middle has been replaced by parcel lockers and a click-and-collect point. Further east, a pharmacy now occupy the unit which used to be a travel agent, and the café in the south-east corner has made way for a cinema.
samples.why: Clear overview of the shift in use · changes presented logically side by side · cohesive devices used well · good vocabulary (outlets, taken over) · largely accurate with one agreement slip.

samples.text:
The floor plans show how the ground floor of a shopping centre changed between 2010 and 2024. Although the physical structure of the building, including the central walkway, the three entrances and the size of every unit, is identical in both years, the mix of tenants has shifted markedly from conventional shops towards leisure, dining and everyday services.

North of the walkway, two of the four units, the clothes shop and the supermarket at the eastern end, have retained their original use. By contrast, the department store in the north-west has been converted into a food court, and the adjacent bookshop has been replaced by a phone shop.

The transformation is more thorough on the southern side, where only the shoe shop survives. Its western neighbour, formerly an electronics store, now houses a gym, while the bank to its east has been turned into a parcel locker and click-and-collect facility. Continuing eastwards, the travel agent has been succeeded by a pharmacy, and the café occupying the south-eastern corner has given way to a cinema. In total, of the nine units shown, only three are used in the same way as in 2010.
samples.why: Excellent overview contrasting fixed structure with changing use · changes sequenced logically along each side · precise summary comparison · sophisticated vocabulary (tenants, succeeded by) · wide range of structures, error-free.
